title: Retrograde Cricopharyngeal Dysfunction: case series and literature review of patients treated with Botulinum Toxin A.
summary: Retrograde cricopharyngeal dysfunction (RCPD) is a condition in which affected individuals are unable to burp, resulting in abdominal bloating, chest pressure, excessive gas, and reduced quality of life. This retrospective study evaluates the clinical presentation, diagnostic work-up, and treatment outcomes of patients with RCPD who received botulinum toxin A injection into the cricopharyngeus muscle. Medical records of three patients are analyzed to determine whether treatment restored the ability to burp, improved symptoms, and caused any adverse effects. The findings may contribute to improving the diagnosis and management of this underrecognized disorder.

interventions.name: Retrospective observational cohort of patients diagnosed with retrograde cricopharyngeal dysfunction (RCPD) who underwent transoral endoscopic injection of 50 units of botulinum toxin A into the cricopharyngeus muscle at a single tertiary academic center. All participants received the same intervent

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with a clinical diagnosis of retrograde cricopharyngeal dysfunction (RCPD).
- Long-standing inability to belch.
- Typical RCPD symptom constellation, including abdominal bloating, excessive gas, thoracic or cervical gurgling, and pressure symptoms.
- Exclusion of structural pathology by clinical evaluation and esophagogastroduodenoscopy.
- Treatment with transoral endoscopic botulinum toxin A injection into the cricopharyngeus muscle.
- Written informed consent for the use of clinical data for research purposes.
Exclusion criteria:
- Clinically relevant dysphagia as the predominant symptom.
- Structural disorders of the esophagus or upper gastrointestinal tract (e.g., strictures, diverticula, tumors, or eosinophilic esophagitis).
- Neuromuscular or neurodegenerative disorders affecting swallowing or esophageal motility.
- Previous surgical or endoscopic intervention involving the esophagus or upper esophageal sphincter.
- Alternative diagnoses explaining the patient's symptom complex.
